title: Intimacy Pact
concept: An agreement for how you ask for closeness and how you say no, so a no never costs either of you anything and what each of you wants doesn’t stay a guess.
whenToUse: Set it up in advance, on a calm day. Bring it out when asking or saying no has started to feel tense, or after a breach that touched this part of the relationship.
steps: Asking? Think first about how it will land for the other person tonight. If you’re declining, you owe nothing. No is enough.
Say out loud: neither of you will punish, sulk or guilt-trip the other for declining. A no costs nothing and needs no reason.

If it helps, agree how you’ll each say a warm no, and an alternative you’d both enjoy, such as holding each other or five minutes of talking. It’s optional and never owed. The other person can say no to the alternative too.
Each of you names what you enjoy and how you like to be approached. Body language can signal interest, but ask, and wait for a clear yes.
Review it every 30 days. The review is about how asking and saying no feel, never about how often. Either of you can skip or postpone it. “Stalled” is never a reason to ask more.

If a no was met with pressure or guilt-tripping, stop here and don’t try to patch intimacy on top. Don’t talk it through in the moment. The one who pressured owns it plainly. The one pressured decides whether, when and with whom to talk. Force, threats, fear or a repeat: use the Help Lines.

phrases.text: I want to be close, just not in that space tonight. Can we hold each other?
Before I think about what I want, I want to know what feels good for you.

working: B says no, plainly. A says “okay” and means it: no cold shoulder, no guilt trip, no sulk at breakfast. The next week, A asks again, lightly.
notWorking: A says no, and B answers with a flat “fine” and the silent treatment. Or B starts without a thought for whether A is up for it. Either one makes the next honest talk harder.
activity: Write the agreement together on the Pacts sheet, and put a real date in the calendar for the 30-day review.
warn: A “no” needs no script, reason or substitute offer. No pact creates an obligation to sex, touch or disclosure. Afraid of your partner, being threatened, or not free to say no? Stop: these tools are not for this. Pressure after a no: stop; don’t talk it through in the moment. The person pressured decides whether, when and with whom to talk. Force, threats, fear or a repeat: Help Lines.
